title: Enterprise SSO (SAML)
summary: Enterprise single sign-on lets employees use one company login for hundreds of SaaS apps, and lets IT cut off all access in one place when someone leaves. With SAML, the app redirects the browser to the company's identity provider, which authenticates the user against the directory with MFA and posts back a signed assertion the app verifies. SCIM provisioning then creates and removes accounts in each app automatically.

walkthrough.title: Open the app
walkthrough.text: An employee visits acme.slack.com. The app sees no session and recognises the company domain, so it uses SSO.

walkthrough.title: Redirect to the identity provider
walkthrough.text: The app redirects the browser to the company's IdP (Okta, Entra ID) with a SAML AuthnRequest: who is asking and where to send the answer.

walkthrough.title: Authenticate with MFA
walkthrough.text: If the employee has no IdP session, the IdP checks their password against the directory and requires MFA (push or a FIDO2 security key). Device and location policies apply.

walkthrough.title: Post a signed assertion
walkthrough.text: The IdP returns an HTML form that auto-posts a SAML Response to the app's Assertion Consumer Service URL. It contains a signed assertion with the user's email, groups, and a short validity window.

walkthrough.title: App validates and creates a session
walkthrough.text: The app verifies the XML signature with the IdP's certificate and checks audience, recipient, expiry, and replay, then logs the user in.

walkthrough.title: Provision with SCIM
walkthrough.text: When HR adds a hire or changes their team, the directory change flows through SCIM: the app's account and group memberships are created or updated before the person's first day.

walkthrough.title: Offboard in one place
walkthrough.text: When someone leaves, disabling them in the directory kills IdP sessions and SCIM deactivates every app account, so access ends everywhere within minutes.

data.label: Employee Browser

input.name: Redirects
input.type: 302 to IdP · auto-POST form back to app

output.name: Login
output.type: Credentials + MFA to the IdP only

responsibilities: Carries messages between the app and the IdP via redirects and posts.
Enters credentials only on the IdP, never on each app.
Holds IdP and app session cookies.

failureModes.mitigation: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) bound to the real domain.

failureModes.scenario: Clock skew on the user's machine
failureModes.impact: Rarely matters: validity is checked on servers.
failureModes.mitigation: Server-side time checks with small allowed skew.

data.label: SaaS App (Service Provider)

output.name: Session
output.type: App session for jane@acme.com with groups

responsibilities: Starts SSO and trusts only assertions signed by the configured IdP.
Maps IdP groups to app roles.
Accepts SCIM calls to create, update, and deactivate users.

failureModes.mitigation: Mature SAML libraries; verify the signed element is the one used.

failureModes.impact: Leavers keep access through a password login.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce SSO-only login for the company domain.

data.label: Identity Provider

input.name: AuthnRequest
input.type: From an app, via the browser

output.name: Assertion
output.type: Signed: subject, email, groups, NotOnOrAfter +5 min

responsibilities: Authenticates users once and issues assertions to every app.
Applies access policies: MFA, device health, location.
Rotates signing certificates and publishes metadata.

failureModes.impact: No one can log in to anything.
failureModes.mitigation: Highly available IdP, long-enough app sessions, break-glass accounts.
Track expiry; publish the new cert in metadata ahead of rotation.

data.label: Corporate Directory
responsibilities: Is the source of truth for who works here and in which teams.
Drives joiner, mover, and leaver changes.

failureModes.mitigation: HR system integration that triggers deprovisioning automatically.

failureModes.impact: Users accumulate access they no longer need.
failureModes.mitigation: Periodic access reviews and role-based groups.

data.label: MFA & Device Trust
responsibilities: Proves possession of a second factor.
Checks the device is managed and patched.

failureModes.mitigation: Number matching or FIDO2; rate-limit prompts.
Second registered key; verified helpdesk recovery.

data.label: SCIM Provisioning

input.name: Change
input.type: User or group change in the directory

responsibilities: Creates app accounts before first login.
Deactivates accounts in every app on offboarding.

failureModes.scenario: SCIM push fails silently for one app
failureModes.impact: Leaver still has an active account there.
failureModes.mitigation: Retry with alerting; periodic full reconciliation.
Deactivate first; transfer ownership before deletion.
